subject: Physics
title: Physics 每日练习卷
scope: Mixed revision: Heat & Gases (specific/latent heat, gas laws, kinetic theory) · Force & Motion · Waves
keyPoints: **Specific heat:** $Q = mc\Delta T$; heat capacity $C = mc$, so $Q = C\Delta T$. Mixing: heat lost by hot body = heat gained by cold body.
**Latent heat:** $Q = m\ell$ at constant temperature. With a heater of power $P$: $Pt = m\ell$ (no heat loss).
**Gas laws:** $pV = nRT$ with $T$ in kelvin ($T = \theta + 273$). Fixed $V$: $\frac{p_1}{T_1} = \frac{p_2}{T_2}$. Number of molecules: $pV = NkT$, $k = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{J K}^{-1}$.
**Kinetic theory:** mean KE $= \frac{3}{2}kT$ depends on $T$ only. $\frac{1}{2}m\overline{c^2} = \frac{3}{2}kT$, so at the same $T$, $c_{rms} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$.
**Kinematics:** $v = u + at$, $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$, $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ (uniform acceleration only).
**Newton's 2nd law:** $F_{net} = ma$. With friction $f$: $F - f = ma$; after the push is removed, friction alone decelerates the body.
**Work and energy:** $W = Fs$; KE $= \frac{1}{2}mv^2$; GPE $= mgh$. Average stopping force: $F \times d$ = total energy removed (include $mgd$ if the body still drops by $d$).
**Waves:** $v = f\lambda$, $T = \frac{1}{f}$. $\lambda$ = distance between adjacent crests. Frequency is set by the source and stays the same in a new medium; $\lambda$ changes with speed.

examples.title: 例 1（加热器与熔解 / heater + latent heat）
examples.question: A 200 W heater melts ice at 0 °C. In 4 minutes, 0.15 kg of ice melts. Find the specific latent heat of fusion. A 0.4 kg metal block at 90 °C is then dropped into 0.5 kg of water at 15 °C; the final temperature is 21 °C. Find the heat capacity of the block. ($c_w = 4200$)
examples.solution:
$Pt = m\ell \Rightarrow \ell = \frac{200 \times 240}{0.15} = 3.2 \times 10^5\ \text{J kg}^{-1}$
Heat lost by block = heat gained by water:
$$C(90 - 21) = 0.5(4200)(21 - 15)$$
$$C = \frac{12600}{69} \approx 183\ \text{J}\ ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$$

examples.title: 例 2（气体定律与分子动理论 / gas laws + kinetic theory）
examples.question: A rigid container of volume $2.0 \times 10^{-3}$ m³ holds gas at $2.0 \times 10^5$ Pa and 27 °C. (a) Find the pressure at 87 °C. (b) Find the number of molecules and their mean KE at 27 °C.
examples.solution:
(a) Fixed $V$: $\frac{p_2}{360} = \frac{2.0 \times 10^5}{300} \Rightarrow p_2 = 2.4 \times 10^5$ Pa
(b) $N = \frac{pV}{kT} = \frac{(2.0 \times 10^5)(2.0 \times 10^{-3})}{(1.38 \times 10^{-23})(300)} = 9.66 \times 10^{22}$
$E_K = \frac{3}{2}kT = \frac{3}{2}(1.38 \times 10^{-23})(300) = 6.21 \times 10^{-21}$ J
A gas with lighter molecules at the same $T$ has the same $E_K$ but a larger $c_{rms}$.

examples.title: 例 3（运动学 + 摩擦 / kinematics with friction）
examples.question: A 5 kg box at rest is pushed by a 30 N horizontal force against a friction of 10 N for 3 s, then the push is removed. Find the maximum speed and the total distance travelled.

examples.title: 例 4（功能原理求平均力 / average force from energy）
examples.question: A 60 kg diver drops from rest 2.0 m above a springboard, then pushes it down 0.30 m before stopping. Estimate the average force on the board. ($g = 9.81$)
examples.solution:
KE on touching = $mgh = 60(9.81)(2.0) = 1177$ J
While pressing down, she also loses GPE $= 60(9.81)(0.30) = 177$ J
$$F(0.30) = 1177 + 177 \Rightarrow F \approx 4.51 \times 10^3\ \text{N}$$
Energy transfer: her KE and GPE become elastic PE of the board.

examples.title: 例 5（波速公式 / wave equation）
examples.question: Adjacent crests of a water wave are 3.0 cm apart and 10 crests pass a point every 2.0 s. Find $f$ and $v$. The wave enters a region where $v = 9.0\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$; find the new wavelength.
examples.solution:
$f = \frac{10}{2.0} = 5.0$ Hz; $v = f\lambda = 5.0 \times 3.0 = 15\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$
Frequency unchanged: $\lambda' = \frac{9.0}{5.0} = 1.8$ cm

questions.stem: 0.50 kg of water at 80 °C is mixed with 0.30 kg of water at 20 °C in a well-insulated container. What is the final temperature?
A fixed mass of gas in a sealed rigid container has pressure $p$ at 27 °C. The gas is heated to 127 °C. What is its new pressure?
questions.solution: Fixed $V$: $\frac{p'}{400} = \frac{p}{300} \Rightarrow p' = \frac{4}{3}p$. Must use kelvin, not °C (127/27 = 4.7 is the trap).

questions.stem: A car moving at 20 m s⁻¹ decelerates uniformly and stops after travelling 50 m. What is the magnitude of its deceleration?
A wave source vibrates at 50 Hz. The distance between two adjacent crests is 4 cm. What is the wave speed?

A block of mass 2.0 kg is initially at rest on a rough horizontal floor. A horizontal force of 10 N pulls the block for 4.0 s and is then removed. The friction acting on the block is 4.0 N throughout.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the block while it is being pulled.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the speed of the block at $t = 4.0$ s and the distance travelled in the first 4.0 s.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Find the distance travelled by the block after the force is removed.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Find the total work done against friction during the whole motion.

questions.stem: A transverse wave travels along a stretched string. The source vibrates at 5.0 Hz and the distance between adjacent crests is 0.80 m.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the speed of the wave.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the period of vibration of a particle on the string.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: The wave passes into a heavier string where its speed is 2.0 m s⁻¹. State its frequency and find its wavelength in the heavier string.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: State one difference between a transverse wave and a longitudinal wave.
parts.answer: Transverse: particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave travel; longitudinal: parallel to it. (1)

questions.source: HKEAA HKDSE Physics Sample Paper (2024 onwards), Paper 1B Q3 (from HKDSE 2020 1B Q5)
questions.stem: Figure 3.1 shows a trampoline gymnast of mass 50 kg performing a straight jump.  Her feet are 1.5 m above the trampoline at the maximum height.  Neglect air resistance and assume that the gymnast maintains this posture throughout the jump.  ($g = 9.81\ \text{m s}^{-2}$)

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the kinetic energy of the gymnast just as her feet touch the trampoline on the way down from her jump.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
After touching the trampoline, the gymnast keeps on moving downward for 0.40 m further before she stops.
Describe the energy transfer to the trampoline by the gymnast after touching the trampoline.
parts.answer: The KE of the gymnast (1) and her loss in GPE (1) are transferred to the elastic potential energy of the trampoline.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Estimate the average force exerted by the gymnast on the trampoline.

questions.source: HKEAA HKDSE Physics Sample Paper (2024 onwards), Paper 1B Q1 (from HKDSE 2021 1B Q1)
questions.stem: A 150 W immersion heater is used to keep the water in a large beaker boiling under standard atmospheric pressure.  In 5 minutes, 0.016 kg of water boils away.  Neglect any heat loss to surroundings.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the specific latent heat of vaporization of water, $\ell$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A student puts a small metal sphere in the boiling water.  After a few minutes, the sphere is quickly transferred to a polystyrene cup containing 100 g of water at a temperature of 20 °C.  The cup of water is stirred gently and its highest temperature attained is 22 °C.
Given:  specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹
Estimate the heat capacity $C$ of the metal sphere.

questions.source: HKEAA HKDSE Physics Sample Paper (2024 onwards), Paper 1B Q10 (from HKDSE 2022 1B Q2)
questions.stem: A sealed tank of volume $6.0 \times 10^{-4}$ m³ contains a monatomic gas A at a pressure of $1.0 \times 10^5$ Pa and at a temperature of 300 K.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Estimate the number of gas molecules in the tank, $N$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Estimate the average kinetic energy of the gas molecules, $E_K$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Another identical tank contains monatomic gas B under the same pressure and temperature.  A molecule of gas B has $\frac{1}{5}$ the mass of a molecule of gas A.
State whether $N$ and $E_K$ of gas B are larger than, smaller than or the same as the corresponding values of those of gas A found in (a).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Given that the root-mean-square speed ($c_{rms}$) of the molecules of gas A is 600 m s⁻¹, estimate $c_{rms}$ of the molecules of gas B.
